// ==== formVm.d.ts ====
import { c as ITypedMessage, I as IMessage, a as IMessageHub } from './messageHub.js';
import { SchedulerLike, Observable } from 'rxjs';
import { R as RelayCommand } from './relayCommand.js';

/**
 * PropertyChangedMessage — emitted when a VM property changes value.
 *
 * See spec/03-messages.md §PropertyChangedMessage.
 */

declare class PropertyChangedMessage<TSender> implements ITypedMessage<TSender> {
    readonly sender: TSender;
    readonly senderName: string;
    readonly propertyName: string;
    private constructor();
    static create<TSender>(sender: TSender, senderName: string, propertyName: string): PropertyChangedMessage<TSender>;
}

/**
 * CollectionChangedMessage — published to the hub when a collection mutates, by
 * ServicedObservableCollection, KeyedServicedObservableCollection,
 * ObservableDictionary and, with the container as sender, by CompositeVM and
 * GroupVM after each local collection change.
 *
 * See spec/21-collections.md §2, spec/01-concepts.md §1.4, ADR-0024 and ADR-0142.
 */

/** Mutation action for a serviced collection message. */
type CollectionMutationAction = "add" | "remove" | "replace" | "move" | "reset";
interface ICollectionChangedMessage<T> extends IMessage {
    readonly action: CollectionMutationAction;
    readonly newItems: readonly T[];
    readonly oldItems: readonly T[];
    readonly index: number;
    /**
     * Source position when supplied. Optional only so pre-v3.16 third-party
     * structural implementations remain assignable; VMx messages always set it.
     */
    readonly oldIndex?: number;
    /**
     * Destination position when supplied. Optional only so pre-v3.16 third-party
     * structural implementations remain assignable; VMx messages always set it.
     */
    readonly newIndex?: number;
}
declare class CollectionChangedMessage<T> implements ICollectionChangedMessage<T> {
    readonly sender: object;
    /** Derived from the sender's constructor name; no separate name field per spec §2.4. */
    get senderName(): string;
    readonly action: CollectionMutationAction;
    readonly newItems: readonly T[];
    readonly oldItems: readonly T[];
    readonly index: number;
    readonly oldIndex: number;
    readonly newIndex: number;
    private constructor();
    static forAdd<T>(sender: object, item: T, index: number): CollectionChangedMessage<T>;
    static forRemove<T>(sender: object, item: T, index: number): CollectionChangedMessage<T>;
    static forReplace<T>(sender: object, newItem: T, oldItem: T, index: number): CollectionChangedMessage<T>;
    static forMove<T>(sender: object, item: T, oldIndex: number, newIndex: number): CollectionChangedMessage<T>;
    static forReset<T>(sender: object): CollectionChangedMessage<T>;
}

/**
 * Dispatcher — paired Rx schedulers for foreground and background work.
 *
 * See spec/11-threading.md for the threading contract.
 */

interface IDispatcher {
    readonly foreground: SchedulerLike;
    readonly background: SchedulerLike;
}
declare class RxDispatcher implements IDispatcher {
    readonly foreground: SchedulerLike;
    readonly background: SchedulerLike;
    constructor(foreground: SchedulerLike, background: SchedulerLike);
    /**
     * Both foreground and background use queueScheduler (synchronous).
     * Suitable for console scripts and unit tests.
     */
    static immediate(): RxDispatcher;
    /**
     * Default browser / Node dispatcher:
     *   foreground → queueScheduler (synchronous trampoline — runs inline,
     *                fair-queued against other queued work)
     *   background → asyncScheduler (macrotask — deferred past the current call
     *                stack AND the microtask queue, so background work does not
     *                starve pending I/O, timers, or paint).
     *
     * VMX-087: background previously used `asapScheduler` (a Promise microtask),
     * which drains before the next macrotask and can starve the event loop —
     * contradicting the "background" intent. `asyncScheduler` is the genuine
     * macrotask deferral. `immediate()` remains fully synchronous for tests.
     */
    static default(): RxDispatcher;
}

/**
 * ObservableList<T> — granular per-mutation event observable list.
 *
 * Exposes four RxJS Subjects for strongly typed mutation streams:
 *   - itemAdded     — emits { item, index } on push/insert
 *   - itemRemoved   — emits { item, index } (index before removal) on remove
 *   - itemReplaced  — emits { newItem, oldItem, index } on replace
 *   - reset         — emits void on clear or batch completion
 *
 * A propertyChanged Subject emits the property name ("Count") after every
 * mutation that changes Count (add and remove; not replace). This ordering
 * is normative per spec §3.3 and ADR-0026.
 *
 * withBatch(callback) invokes the callback, suppresses granular events, and
 * fires a single reset on completion (ref-counted for nested calls).
 *
 * See spec/21-collections.md §3 and ADR-0026.
 */

interface ItemAddedEvent<T> {
    readonly item: T;
    readonly index: number;
}
interface ItemRemovedEvent<T> {
    readonly item: T;
    /** Index of the item before it was removed. */
    readonly index: number;
}
interface ItemReplacedEvent<T> {
    readonly newItem: T;
    readonly oldItem: T;
    readonly index: number;
}
declare class ObservableList<T> {
    #private;
    /** Emits when an item is added. Payload: { item, index }. */
    get itemAdded(): Observable<ItemAddedEvent<T>>;
    /** Emits when an item is removed. Payload: { item, index } (index before removal). */
    get itemRemoved(): Observable<ItemRemovedEvent<T>>;
    /** Emits when an item is replaced. Payload: { newItem, oldItem, index }. */
    get itemReplaced(): Observable<ItemReplacedEvent<T>>;
    /** Emits (void) on clear or when a batch completes with mutations. */
    get reset(): Observable<void>;
    /**
     * Emits the property name whenever a property changes.
     * Emits "Count" after every add and remove (not after replace).
     * Ordering: granular event fires before propertyChanged("Count") — normative.
     */
    get propertyChanged(): Observable<string>;
    get length(): number;
    at(index: number): T | undefined;
    toArray(): T[];
    [Symbol.iterator](): IterableIterator<T>;
    /** Append an item to the end of the list. */
    push(item: T): void;
    /**
     * Insert an item at the given index (`length` appends).
     * Throws RangeError if index is out of bounds — `splice` would otherwise
     * silently normalize/clamp while the emitted payload carried the raw index.
     */
    insert(index: number, item: T): void;
    /** Remove and return the last item, or undefined if empty. */
    pop(): T | undefined;
    /**
     * Remove the item at *index*.
     * Throws RangeError if index is out of bounds.
     */
    removeAt(index: number): void;
    /**
     * Remove the first occurrence of *item*.
     * Returns true if the item was found and removed, false otherwise.
     */
    remove(item: T): boolean;
    /**
     * Replace the item at *index* with *newItem*.
     * Throws RangeError if index is out of bounds.
     */
    replace(index: number, newItem: T): void;
    /**
     * Replace the complete contents from a snapshot of *items*.
     * Empty-to-empty is the only no-op; every other replacement emits one reset,
     * followed by "Count" only when the cardinality changed.
     */
    replaceAll(items: Iterable<T>): void;
    /** Remove all items and emit reset (and "Count" when it changed). */
    clear(): void;
    /**
     * Execute *callback*, suppressing granular events during execution.
     * On completion of the outermost batch (ref-counted), a single reset fires
     * if any mutations occurred. If the count changed, propertyChanged("Count")
     * also fires (spec §3.3).
     */
    withBatch(callback: () => void): void;
}

/** Consumer-supplied async persister delegate. Throw on failure. */
type Persister<TM> = (model: TM) => Promise<void>;
/**
 * Optional custom snapshot function. Defaults to `structuredClone`. Pair a
 * custom implementation with a matching {@link ModelEquals} predicate so
 * snapshot, revert, and dirty-tracking semantics stay aligned.
 */
type Snapshotter<TM> = (model: TM) => TM;
/** Derives the next pristine model from the captured, persisted value. */
type ResetOnApproved<TM> = (model: TM) => TM;
/** Field-level validator. Return a string error, or null/undefined when valid. */
type FieldValidator<TM> = (model: TM) => string | null | undefined;
/** Model-level validator returning field-name errors. Null entries clear fields. */
type ModelValidator<TM> = (model: TM) => Record<string, string | null | undefined>;
/**
 * Optional custom equality predicate for dirty-tracking. Returns `true` when
 * `a` and `b` are considered the *same* (i.e. the form is clean). Defaults to
 * {@link deepEquals}.
 */
type ModelEquals<TM> = (a: TM, b: TM) => boolean;
/** Constructor options for FormVM. */
interface FormVMOptions<TM> {
    /** Initial domain model; also becomes the initial snapshot. */
    initial: TM;
    /** Async persist delegate. Throw on failure. */
    persister: Persister<TM>;
    /** Message hub. Defaults to NullMessageHub.INSTANCE. */
    hub?: IMessageHub;
    /**
     * When true, `approveCommand.canExecute()` returns false when `isDirty` is false.
     * Default: false.
     */
    strict?: boolean;
    /**
     * Custom snapshot function. Defaults to `structuredClone` — a structured
     * deep clone; nested references are independent between Model and Snapshot.
     * Supply a custom snapshotter if you need shallow semantics or your model
     * contains values structuredClone cannot serialize, and pair it with a
     * matching `equals` predicate. A built-in clone failure is rethrown with the
     * FormVM phase and, when safely determinable, the owning top-level field;
     * the native error remains available as `cause`. Errors from a supplied
     * snapshotter pass through unchanged.
     */
    snapshotter?: Snapshotter<TM>;
    /**
     * Custom equality predicate for dirty-tracking (`isDirty = !equals(model,
     * snapshot)`). Defaults to {@link deepEquals}, a structural deep-equal that
     * matches what the default `structuredClone` snapshotter clones (handles
     * Date/Map/Set/BigInt/circular refs). Supply your own to compare on a subset
     * of fields or with reference semantics.
     */
    equals?: ModelEquals<TM>;
    /** Optional field validators keyed by idiomatic field/property name. */
    validators?: Record<string, FieldValidator<TM>>;
    /** Optional model-level validator returning field-name errors. */
    modelValidator?: ModelValidator<TM>;
    /** Optional post-persist callback that derives the next pristine model. */
    resetOnApproved?: ResetOnApproved<TM>;
}
/**
 * ViewModel that wraps a mutable domain model with an edit lifecycle.
 *
 * Captures a snapshot at construction; allows mutation via {@link setModel};
 * provides {@link denyCommand} (revert) and {@link approveCommand} (persist).
 */
declare class FormVM<TM> {
    #private;
    readonly denyCommand: RelayCommand;
    readonly approveCommand: RelayCommand;
    /**
     * Entry point for the immutable fluent builder. Mirrors the
     * `.builder()` convention used by the other VM family members
     * (`ComponentVM`, `CompositeVM`, …). See ADR-0035 §2 FV1 / FV2.
     */
    static builder<TM>(): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    constructor(options: FormVMOptions<TM>);
    /** Live, editable model. Set via {@link setModel} to mutate. */
    get model(): TM;
    /** Read-only snapshot captured at construction (until next approve). */
    get snapshot(): TM;
    /**
     * True when `model` is structurally not equal to `snapshot`.
     * Uses the injectable `equals` predicate (default {@link deepEquals}).
     */
    get isDirty(): boolean;
    /** Current validation errors keyed by field/property name. */
    get errors(): Record<string, string>;
    /** True when the current model has no validation errors. */
    get isValid(): boolean;
    /** Observable that emits the current model after each successful persist. */
    get onApproved(): Observable<TM>;
    /**
     * Observable that surfaces the error thrown by the persister when the approve
     * COMMAND (`approveCommand.execute()`) fails. That path is fire-and-forget
     * (`RelayCommand.execute` is `void`), so a rejection cannot propagate to the
     * caller — it is emitted here instead of being swallowed (VMX-008). The
     * awaitable {@link approveAsync} path keeps its throw behavior; await it
     * directly to handle the failure inline. Completes on {@link dispose}.
     */
    get approveErrors(): Observable<unknown>;
    /** Emits only when the effective validation error map changes. */
    get errorsChanged(): Observable<Record<string, string>>;
    /** Return the current validation error for a field, if any. */
    fieldError(field: string): string | undefined;
    /**
     * Replaces the current model. May change `isDirty`; in strict mode fires
     * `approveCommand.canExecuteChanged` on dirty transitions.
     * A call begun after disposal returns before inspecting the candidate.
     *
     * The update is failure-atomic (§5.4): the equality comparisons and the
     * validators run before anything is committed. If one throws, the error
     * propagates and the form is unchanged, with nothing published. If a
     * callback disposes the form or commits another update, this call commits
     * and publishes nothing.
     *
     * A call made from `resetOnApproved`, the approval's snapshotter or
     * validators, or a settlement `errorsChanged` or `canExecuteChanged`
     * observer is queued (§5.3, ADR-0174). It runs the same preparation first,
     * so a failure still reaches the caller, but it commits and publishes
     * nothing until it replays after `onApproved`.
     *
     * A call made from a preparation callback of another `setModel` or deny,
     * or from an `errorsChanged` observer of one, commits at once but returns
     * before its notifications. The outermost update sends them before it
     * returns, and drops them once the form is disposed (§5.4, ADR-0180).
     */
    setModel(model: TM): void;
    /**
     * Awaitable approve flow. Invokes the persister, advances `snapshot` on success,
     * and fires `onApproved`. Throws when the persister throws (no state mutation).
     * Only one approval runs at a time: a call made while another is in flight
     * returns without persisting, mutating, throwing, or emitting (§5.3).
     *
     * A `setModel` or deny queued during the post-persist commit or settlement
     * replays after `onApproved` (or after a failed commit's settlement). If a
     * replay throws, the later ones still run, and the first replay failure is
     * thrown here after the last one, unless the approval already failed.
     *
     * A call made from a preparation callback of a `setModel` or deny, or from
     * an `errorsChanged` observer of one, is admitted at once. Its
     * `canExecuteChanged` and its persister call wait for the outermost update
     * (§5.4, ADR-0180). A `dispose()` before the persister starts prevents the
     * call, and the returned promise then resolves (§10).
     */
    approveAsync(): Promise<void>;
    /** Complete the `onApproved` observable and dispose resources. Idempotent. */
    dispose(): void;
}
/**
 * Immutable fluent builder for {@link FormVM}.
 *
 * Required setters: {@link initial}, {@link persister}.
 * Optional setters: {@link hub}, {@link strict}, {@link snapshotter},
 * {@link equals}.
 *
 * Each setter returns a NEW builder instance (BLD-001). `build()`
 * validates the required fields and throws {@link BuilderValidationError}
 * on the first missing one (BLD-002).
 */
declare class FormVMBuilder<TM> {
    #private;
    constructor(from?: FormVMBuilder<TM>);
    /** Set the required initial domain model. */
    initial(value: TM): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /** Set the required async persister delegate `(model) => Promise<void>`. */
    persister(value: Persister<TM>): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /** Set the optional message hub (default: {@link NullMessageHub.INSTANCE}). */
    hub(value: IMessageHub): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /**
     * Enable strict mode (`approveCommand.canExecute()` returns false when
     * `isDirty` is false). Default: `false`.
     */
    strict(value: boolean): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /**
     * Set a custom snapshot function (default: `structuredClone`). The default
     * requires a structured-cloneable model and reports phase/field context on
     * failure. Pair a custom snapshotter with {@link equals}; custom errors pass
     * through unchanged.
     */
    snapshotter(value: Snapshotter<TM>): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /** Set a custom dirty-tracking equality predicate (default: {@link deepEquals}). */
    equals(value: ModelEquals<TM>): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /** Register a field validator. The returned builder is a new instance. */
    validator(field: string, value: FieldValidator<TM>): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /** Register a model-level validator returning field-name errors. */
    modelValidator(value: ModelValidator<TM>): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /** Derive the next pristine model after persistence succeeds. */
    resetOnApproved(value: ResetOnApproved<TM>): FormVMBuilder<TM>;
    /**
     * Validate required fields and construct a {@link FormVM}.
     *
     * @throws {BuilderValidationError} If `initial` or `persister` is not set.
     */
    build(): FormVM<TM>;
}

export { CollectionChangedMessage as C, FormVM as F, type IDispatcher as I, ObservableList as O, PropertyChangedMessage as P, type ResetOnApproved as R, type Snapshotter as S, type CollectionMutationAction as a, FormVMBuilder as b, type FormVMOptions as c, type ICollectionChangedMessage as d, type ItemAddedEvent as e, type ItemRemovedEvent as f, type ItemReplacedEvent as g, type Persister as h, RxDispatcher as i };

/**
 * Package version, matching package.json.
 *
 * Kept in sync with package.json by scripts/check-version-sync.mjs, which runs
 * as part of `prebuild` and `prepack`. Update both when releasing.
 */
declare const __version__ = "3.31.0";
/** Minimum spec version this package implements (see spec/VERSION). */
declare const __minSpecVersion__ = "3.30.0";

/**
 * Builder validation exception type.
 *
 * Raised by a builder's `build()` method when a required field is missing.
 * Mirrors `BuilderValidationError` in the Python flavor and
 * `BuilderValidationException` in the C# flavor (idiomatic `Error` suffix
 * per ADR-0006).
 *
 * See spec/10-builders.md §Validation.
 */
declare class BuilderValidationError extends Error {
    /** Name of the first missing required field that caused the failure. */
    readonly missingField: string;
    constructor(missingField: string, message?: string);
}

/**
 * ConstructionStatus — five-state lifecycle enum.
 *
 * Values match the Python and C# counterparts so that JSON fixtures
 * round-trip cleanly across language boundaries.
 *
 * See spec/02-lifecycle.md for the full state-machine contract.
 */
declare enum ConstructionStatus {
    /** Terminal state. Once entered, cannot leave. */
    Disposed = 0,
    /** Transient state during destruct(). */
    Destructing = 1,
    /** Initial state of a freshly built VM. */
    Destructed = 2,
    /** Transient state during construct(). */
    Constructing = 3,
    /** Ready-to-use state. */
    Constructed = 4
}

/**
 * StatusTransitionError — raised when a lifecycle operation is forbidden.
 *
 * See spec/02-lifecycle.md §Invariants 3 and 5.
 */

declare class StatusTransitionError extends Error {
    readonly currentStatus: ConstructionStatus;
    readonly attemptedOperation: string;
    constructor(currentStatus: ConstructionStatus, attemptedOperation: string);
}

/**
 * Lifecycle transition validator.
 *
 * Loads the lifecycle-transitions.json fixture via a static TypeScript JSON
 * import so the data is bundled into the dist by tsup/esbuild at build time.
 * This makes the module browser-safe (no runtime built-in Node module
 * resolution required), and removes the previous fs-search of candidate
 * paths.
 *
 * Public surface:
 *   isLegal(current, operation) → boolean
 *   requireTransition(current, operation) → void (throws StatusTransitionError)
 *   finalState(current, operation) → ConstructionStatus
 */

declare function isLegal(current: ConstructionStatus, operation: string): boolean;
declare function requireTransition(current: ConstructionStatus, operation: string): void;
declare function finalState(current: ConstructionStatus, operation: string): ConstructionStatus;

/**
 * propertyValueChangedMessagesFor — value-returning observable over PropertyChangedMessage.
 *
 * Convenience helper over the message hub. Instead of filtering the full message stream and
 * extracting the sender property manually, this function returns an Observable<unknown> that
 * emits the current value of the named property on the sender each time a matching
 * PropertyChangedMessage arrives.
 *
 * This helper is informative-only (ADR-0032); the underlying `messages` stream on the hub
 * is the conformance-tested contract.
 *
 * See spec/03-messages.md §"Convenience helpers".
 */

/** Minimal hub shape required by the helper. */
interface IHubLike$1 {
    readonly messages: Observable<IMessage>;
}
/**
 * Returns an observable that emits the current value of `propertyName` on `source`
 * each time a matching `PropertyChangedMessage` arrives on the hub.
 *
 * @param hub - The message hub to filter.
 * @param source - The specific sender instance to watch (identity check).
 * @param propertyName - Name of the property to observe.
 * @returns Cold observable of property values (snapshotted at delivery time).
 */
declare function propertyValueChangedMessagesFor<TSource extends object>(hub: IHubLike$1, source: TSource, propertyName: keyof TSource & string): Observable<unknown>;

/**
 * whenPropertyChanged — typed observable of PropertyChangedMessage events for a
 * specific sender + property (VMX-017).
 *
 * Replaces the hand-wired
 * `hub.messages.pipe(filter(m => m instanceof PropertyChangedMessage && m.sender === x && m.propertyName === "P"))`
 * filter that otherwise gets copy-pasted into every cross-VM binding. Unlike
 * {@link propertyValueChangedMessagesFor} (which maps to the property *value*),
 * this emits the matching message so the subscriber can react and read whatever
 * state it needs — mirroring the C# `IMessageHub.WhenPropertyChanged` helper.
 *
 * Informative-only (ADR-0032); the underlying `messages` stream is the
 * conformance-tested contract.
 *
 * See spec/03-messages.md §"Convenience helpers".
 */

/** Minimal hub shape required by the helper. */
interface IHubLike {
    readonly messages: Observable<IMessage>;
}
/**
 * Returns the stream of {@link PropertyChangedMessage} events published to `hub`
 * by `sender` for the property named `propertyName`. Sender identity is compared
 * by reference.
 *
 * Pass an array to watch several properties of one sender (spec/03 §7.2,
 * ADR-0160): `whenPropertyChanged(hub, chart, ["plot", "range"])`. A message
 * matches when its `propertyName` equals any of the names. Each subscription
 * makes one subscription to `hub.messages`, and each matching message is
 * emitted once, in hub order, even when its name appears more than once in the
 * array. The names are copied when the function is called, so a later change
 * to the array has no effect. A single string behaves as before.
 *
 * @param hub - The message hub to observe.
 * @param sender - The sender instance to match (identity check).
 * @param propertyName - Name of the property to match, or a non-empty array of
 *   names to match.
 * @throws RangeError if `propertyName` is an empty array.
 */
declare function whenPropertyChanged(hub: IHubLike, sender: object, propertyName: string | readonly string[]): Observable<PropertyChangedMessage<unknown>>;

/**
 * ViewModelType enum and IComponentVM interface.
 *
 * See spec/01-concepts.md §IComponentVM baseline.
 */

declare enum ViewModelType {
    Component = "Component",
    ReadOnlyComponent = "ReadOnlyComponent",
    Composite = "Composite",
    Group = "Group",
    Aggregate = "Aggregate"
}
/**
 * The order in which a `GroupVM` or `CompositeVM` destructs and disposes its
 * children (spec/02 §6, ADR-0161).
 *
 * - `"insertion"` (default) walks the children in their current order, first
 *   child first, as the construct walk does.
 * - `"reverse"` walks them last child first, so a child that depends on an
 *   earlier sibling is torn down before that sibling.
 *
 * Construct order is the same for both values.
 */
type ChildOrder = "insertion" | "reverse";
/** Shared baseline every VMx viewmodel exposes. */
interface IComponentVM {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly hint: string;
    readonly type: ViewModelType;
    readonly isCurrent: boolean;
    readonly isConstructed: boolean;
    readonly status: ConstructionStatus;
    readonly hub: IMessageHub;
    readonly selectCommand: ICommand;
    readonly deselectCommand: ICommand;
    readonly selectNextCommand: ICommand;
    readonly selectPreviousCommand: ICommand;
    readonly reconstructCommand: ICommand;
    canConstruct(): boolean;
    construct(): void;
    canDestruct(): boolean;
    destruct(): void;
    canReconstruct(): boolean;
    reconstruct(): void;
    dispose(): void;
    canSelect(): boolean;
    select(): void;
    canDeselect(): boolean;
    deselect(): void;
    /** INPC-equivalent: emits property names when properties change. */
    readonly propertyChanged: Observable<string>;
}
/**
 * Modeled variant adds a typed Model property. Per spec/09-forwarding.md §1 the
 * modeled component's `model` is settable (read-only only on the readonly
 * component); the forwarding decorator must therefore delegate the setter too.
 */
interface IComponentVMOf<M> extends IComponentVM {
    model: M;
    readonly modeledHint: string;
    republishModel(): void;
}

interface SubscribeValueOptions<TValue> {
    readonly equality?: (current: TValue, next: TValue) => boolean;
    readonly fireImmediately?: boolean;
}
declare function subscribeValue<TSource extends IComponentVM, TValue>(source: TSource, selector: (source: TSource) => TValue, callback: (current: TValue, previous: TValue) => void, options?: SubscribeValueOptions<TValue>): Subscription;

/**
 * ConstructionStatusChangedMessage — emitted on every legal lifecycle transition.
 *
 * See spec/03-messages.md §ConstructionStatusChangedMessage.
 */

declare class ConstructionStatusChangedMessage implements IMessage {
    readonly sender: object;
    readonly senderName: string;
    readonly status: ConstructionStatus;
    private constructor();
    static create(sender: object, senderName: string, status: ConstructionStatus): ConstructionStatusChangedMessage;
}

/**
 * TreeStructureChangedMessage — published on the message hub when a
 * HierarchicalVM subtree changes structurally (add / remove / reparent).
 *
 * See spec/18-hierarchical-vm.md §6 and ADR-0028 §3.4.
 */

/** Discriminated union for the structural mutation that occurred. */
type TreeStructureChange = "added" | "removed" | "reparented";
/**
 * Message published when a HierarchicalVM's children list mutates.
 *
 * @param TSource - Type of the node whose subtree changed.
 * @param TAffected - Type of the node added, removed, or reparented.
 */
declare class TreeStructureChangedMessage<TSource, TAffected> implements IMessage {
    readonly sender: TSource;
    readonly senderName: string;
    readonly change: TreeStructureChange;
    readonly affected: TAffected;
    /** Index in the children list at which the change occurred; -1 when not applicable. */
    readonly index: number;
    constructor(sender: TSource, senderName: string, change: TreeStructureChange, affected: TAffected, index: number);
}

declare function isPropertyChanged(message: IMessage): message is PropertyChangedMessage<unknown>;
declare function isPropertyChanged<TSender>(message: IMessage, constraints: {
    readonly sender: TSender;
    readonly propertyName?: string | undefined;
}): message is PropertyChangedMessage<TSender>;
declare function isPropertyChanged(message: IMessage, constraints: {
    readonly propertyName?: string | undefined;
}): message is PropertyChangedMessage<unknown>;
declare function isCollectionChanged(message: IMessage): message is CollectionChangedMessage<unknown>;
declare function isCollectionChanged(message: IMessage, constraints: {
    readonly source?: object | undefined;
    readonly action?: CollectionMutationAction | undefined;
}): message is CollectionChangedMessage<unknown>;
declare function isConstructionStatusChanged(message: IMessage): message is ConstructionStatusChangedMessage;
declare function isConstructionStatusChanged(message: IMessage, constraints: {
    readonly sender?: object | undefined;
    readonly status?: ConstructionStatus | undefined;
}): message is ConstructionStatusChangedMessage;
declare function isTreeStructureChanged(message: IMessage): message is TreeStructureChangedMessage<unknown, unknown>;
declare function isTreeStructureChanged<TSender>(message: IMessage, constraints: {
    readonly sender: TSender;
    readonly change?: TreeStructureChange | undefined;
}): message is TreeStructureChangedMessage<TSender, unknown>;
declare function isTreeStructureChanged(message: IMessage, constraints: {
    readonly change?: TreeStructureChange | undefined;
}): message is TreeStructureChangedMessage<unknown, unknown>;

/**
 * CollectionChangedEvent — immutable payload emitted on collection mutations.
 *
 * Mirrors WPF's NotifyCollectionChangedEventArgs shape.
 * Action is one of "add" | "remove" | "move" | "reset".
 */
type CollectionChangedAction = "add" | "remove" | "move" | "reset";
interface CollectionChangedEvent {
    readonly action: CollectionChangedAction;
    readonly newItems: readonly unknown[];
    readonly newIndex: number;
    readonly oldItems: readonly unknown[];
    readonly oldIndex: number;
}
declare function makeCollectionChangedEvent(action: CollectionChangedAction, opts?: {
    newItems?: readonly unknown[];
    newIndex?: number;
    oldItems?: readonly unknown[];
    oldIndex?: number;
}): CollectionChangedEvent;

/**
 * BatchUpdateHandle — ref-counted disposable for batch collection mutations.
 *
 * See spec/06-composite-vm.md §Batch updates (spec v1.1).
 */
/** Internal interface implemented by containers that support batching. */
interface IBatchable {
    _exitBatch(): void;
}
declare class BatchUpdateHandle {
    #private;
    constructor(owner: IBatchable);
    dispose(): void;
    /** Support `using` resource management (TC39 stage 3 / TypeScript 5.2). */
    [Symbol.dispose](): void;
}

/** Minimal parent interface used by a child for selection delegation. */
interface IParentVM {
    readonly supportsChildSelection: boolean;
    readonly currentChild: ComponentVMBase | null;
    selectChild(vm: ComponentVMBase): void;
    deselectChild(vm: ComponentVMBase): void;
}
/** @internal Ownership-capable parent link used only by VMx containers. */
interface IOwningParentVM extends IParentVM {
    readonly owner: ComponentVMBase;
    readonly ownerParent: IOwningParentVM | null;
    containsChild(vm: ComponentVMBase): boolean;
    detachForTransfer(vm: ComponentVMBase): ParentTransfer;
}
/** @internal One-shot staged old-parent removal. */
declare class ParentTransfer {
    #private;
    private readonly commitAction;
    private readonly rollbackAction;
    constructor(commitAction: () => void, rollbackAction: () => void);
    commit(): void;
    rollback(): void;
}
interface DisposableResource {
    dispose(): void;
}
interface UnsubscribableResource {
    unsubscribe(): void;
}
type OwnedResource = (() => void) | DisposableResource | UnsubscribableResource;
declare abstract class ComponentVMBase {
    #private;
    get _parent(): IOwningParentVM | null;
    set _parent(value: IOwningParentVM | null);
    /** @internal Rejects nested ownership changes until the active mutation commits. */
    _ownershipInProgress: boolean;
    /** @internal Canonical component identity shared by forwarding decorators. */
    get _ownershipIdentity(): ComponentVMBase;
    constructor(opts: {
        name: string;
        /** Defaults to `""`. */
        hint?: string;
        hub: IMessageHub;
        dispatcher: IDispatcher;
        onConstruct?: (() => void) | null;
        onDestruct?: (() => void) | null;
        background?: boolean;
    });
    get name(): string;
    get hint(): string;
    get hub(): IMessageHub;
    abstract get type(): ViewModelType;
    get status(): ConstructionStatus;
    get isConstructed(): boolean;
    get isCurrent(): boolean;
    _setIsCurrent(value: boolean): void;
    /**
     * Internal: commits the current flag without publishing it and reports
     * whether it changed. A composite commits `current` and both flags before it
     * publishes any of them (spec/06 §4.3 rule 1, ADR-0173).
     */
    _commitIsCurrent(value: boolean): boolean;
    /** Internal: publishes a flag change that `_commitIsCurrent` reported. */
    _publishIsCurrent(): void;
    get propertyChanged(): Observable<string>;
    protected _raisePropertyChanged(propertyName: string): void;
    /** Publish one hub message, then one VM-local notification for assigned state. */
    protected _notifyPropertyChanged(propertyName: string): void;
    get selectCommand(): RelayCommand;
    get deselectCommand(): RelayCommand;
    get selectNextCommand(): RelayCommand;
    get selectPreviousCommand(): RelayCommand;
    get reconstructCommand(): RelayCommand;
    canConstruct(): boolean;
    canDestruct(): boolean;
    canReconstruct(): boolean;
    construct(): void;
    destruct(): void;
    reconstruct(): void;
    /**
     * Stop waiting for a pending child transition without settling this VM, so
     * a child reaching Disposed does not roll this VM back first. The VMx
     * containers do this through `_beginDisposeCascade` at the start of
     * `dispose()`, which also closes hook admission.
     */
    protected _abandonChildTransition(): void;
    /**
     * @internal Unsupported: not part of the public API; containers only.
     * Start the inline dispose cascade (spec/02 §7.2, ADR-0175). A container
     * calls this at the start of `dispose()`, before it disposes its first
     * child. It abandons a pending child wait, as `_abandonChildTransition`
     * does, and closes hook admission: until this VM publishes Disposed, a
     * `construct()`, `destruct()` or `reconstruct()` call throws the
     * `StatusTransitionError` of a Disposed VM, no hook runs, and no status
     * other than Disposed commits.
     */
    protected _beginDisposeCascade(): void;
    /**
     * Construct (`construct === true`) or destruct the given child VMs as part
     * of this VM's own transition (spec/02-lifecycle.md §6.1, ADR-0162). A leaf
     * VM that holds member VMs calls this from its `_onConstruct` or
     * `_onDestruct` override, so the members settle before this VM publishes
     * `Constructed` or `Destructed`:
     *
     * - The walk takes `children` in the order given, one child at a time: a
     *   child starts only after the previous child settled. To destruct in
     *   reverse order, pass a reversed list.
     * - A child already at the target status is skipped. A child already in the
     *   transient status (`Constructing` / `Destructing`) is joined: the walk
     *   waits for it and does not start it again.
     * - A child left in its transient status (a background child) defers this
     *   VM's terminal status. This VM stays `Constructing` / `Destructing` until
     *   the child settles, and then the walk continues.
     * - A child that settles at any other status (its hook failed, or it was
     *   disposed) stops the walk and rolls this VM back to its prior settled
     *   status. Siblings that already reached the target are not undone. A
     *   synchronous failure is thrown from `construct()` / `destruct()`.
     * - `after` runs exactly once, after every child reached the target and
     *   before this VM publishes its terminal status. A throwing `after` rolls
     *   this VM back like a child failure.
     *
     * Call it only from this VM's own construct or destruct hook, including the
     * two phases of `reconstruct()`. A call from anywhere else throws an `Error`
     * and starts no child. `children` is read lazily, one child at a time.
     *
     * @example
     * ```ts
     * protected override _onConstruct(): void {
     *   super._onConstruct();
     *   this._transitionChildren([this.chart, this.table], true);
     * }
     * protected override _onDestruct(): void {
     *   this._transitionChildren([this.table, this.chart], false, () => super._onDestruct());
     * }
     * ```
     */
    protected _transitionChildren(children: Iterable<ComponentVMBase>, construct: boolean, after?: () => void): void;
    /**
     * @internal Unsupported: not part of the public API; containers only.
     * Container form of {@link _transitionChildren}. A child in
     * `joined` already started this transition (factory population): it is
     * joined and its settled status is final, so it is never restarted.
     * `joined` is read live, so a container can extend its walk while it runs.
     */
    protected _transitionChildrenJoining(children: Iterable<ComponentVMBase>, construct: boolean, after: (() => void) | undefined, joined: ReadonlySet<ComponentVMBase>): void;
    dispose(): void;
    canSelect(): boolean;
    select(): void;
    canDeselect(): boolean;
    deselect(): void;
    protected _onConstruct(): void;
    protected _onDestruct(): void;
    protected _onDispose(): void;
    protected own<T extends OwnedResource>(resource: T): T;
    /**
     * Register `member` as a member VM that this VM disposes (spec/02 §7.1,
     * ADR-0162). `dispose()` disposes the members in registration order before
     * this VM publishes `Disposed`, so a member and its own children reach
     * `Disposed` first. Every member is disposed even when one throws; the
     * first failure is thrown from `dispose()` after the rest of the teardown.
     *
     * A member is not a container child: it has no parent link, takes no part
     * in selection, and is not constructed with this VM. Pass it to
     * {@link _transitionChildren} from the construct and destruct hooks to
     * transition it with this VM.
     *
     * A member registered while this VM is disposing or already disposed is
     * disposed at once, and a failure of that disposal is thrown from this
     * call. Registering this VM itself throws an `Error`. Returns `member`, so
     * a field can register it inline:
     * `readonly chart = this.ownMember(new ChartVM(...))`.
     */
    protected ownMember<T extends ComponentVMBase>(member: T): T;
    protected _setStatus(newStatus: ConstructionStatus): void;
    protected get _hub(): IMessageHub;
    protected get _dispatcher(): IDispatcher;
    protected get _name(): string;
    /** Schedule work on the foreground scheduler. */
    protected _scheduleForeground(work: () => void): void;
}

/** Shared ordered, observable child-collection capability without selection. */
interface IVmCollection<VM extends ComponentVMBase> extends Iterable<VM> {
    readonly count: number;
    readonly collectionChanged: Observable<CollectionChangedEvent>;
    at(index: number): VM;
    add(item: VM): void;
    insert(index: number, item: VM): void;
    remove(item: VM): boolean;
    removeAt(index: number): void;
    setAt(index: number, value: VM): void;
    clear(): void;
    move(fromIndex: number, toIndex: number): void;
    batchUpdate(): BatchUpdateHandle;
}
/** VM collection that additionally owns a current-child selection slot. */
interface ISelectableVmCollection<VM extends ComponentVMBase> extends IVmCollection<VM> {
    current: VM | null;
    selectComponent(vm: VM): void;
    deselectComponent(vm: VM): void;
    canSelectComponent(vm: VM): boolean;
}

/** Read-only ordered membership with payload-free structural notifications. */
interface ObservableMembershipSource<T> {
    snapshot(): readonly T[];
    subscribeMembership(callback: () => void): Subscription;
}

/** Provenance for one aggregate notification. */
declare enum AggregateChangeReason {
    Initial = "initial",
    Membership = "membership",
    Item = "item",
    Batch = "batch"
}
/** Provenance-only aggregate envelope. */
type AggregateChange<T extends object> = {
    readonly reason: AggregateChangeReason.Initial | AggregateChangeReason.Membership | AggregateChangeReason.Batch;
    readonly item?: never;
} | {
    readonly reason: AggregateChangeReason.Item;
    readonly item: T;
};
interface AggregateObserveOptions {
    readonly emitInitial?: boolean;
}
/**
 * Follows live source membership and fans in one selected stream per distinct
 * current object identity.
 */
declare class AggregateChangeStream<T extends object> {
    #private;
    constructor(source: ObservableMembershipSource<T>, observeItem: (item: T) => Observable<unknown>);
    /** Return the hot output with an optional atomic subscriber-local seed. */
    observe(options?: AggregateObserveOptions): Observable<AggregateChange<T>>;
    /** Run an action in a nested, ref-counted aggregate coalescing scope. */
    withBatch<TResult>(action: () => TResult): TResult;
    /** Detach owned subscriptions and complete output. Idempotent. */
    dispose(): void;
    /** Observe the standard VM-local property-change stream. */
    static forComponents<TComponent extends ComponentVMBase>(source: ObservableMembershipSource<TComponent>): AggregateChangeStream<TComponent>;
}

/**
 * ServicedObservableCollection<T> — observable array that optionally publishes
 * CollectionChangedMessage events to an IMessageHub.
 *
 * When no hub is injected, the class behaves like a plain observable collection
 * (local RxJS Subject emits events; no publication, no errors).
 *
 * Ownership stays with the caller: removing, replacing, or clearing an item does
 * not call dispose/destruct or any VM lifecycle method on that item.
 *
 * See spec/21-collections.md §2, ADR-0024, and ADR-0096.
 */

declare class ServicedObservableCollection<T> implements ObservableMembershipSource<T> {
    #private;
    constructor(hub?: IMessageHub | null);
    /** Hot observable of CollectionChangedMessage events. */
    get collectionChanged(): Observable<CollectionChangedMessage<T>>;
    get length(): number;
    /** Return the item at *index*. */
    at(index: number): T | undefined;
    /** Return a shallow copy of the backing array. */
    toArray(): T[];
    [Symbol.iterator](): IterableIterator<T>;
    snapshot(): readonly T[];
    subscribeMembership(callback: () => void): Subscription;
    /** Append *item* to the end. */
    push(item: T): void;
    /** Remove and return the last item, or undefined if empty. */
    pop(): T | undefined;
    /** Remove the first indexOf match for *item*. */
    remove(item: T): boolean;
    /** Remove the item at *index*. */
    removeAt(index: number): void;
    /**
     * Remove *count* items starting at *start* and optionally insert *newItems*.
     * Emits a Reset message (coarse-grained) for any multi-item splice.
     * For single-item operations (no inserts, count=1) emits a Remove.
    */
    splice(start: number, deleteCount?: number, ...newItems: T[]): T[];
    /** Replace the item at *index*, emitting even when the value is identical. */
    replace(index: number, newItem: T): void;
    /** Source-compatible alias for replace. */
    setAt(index: number, newItem: T): void;
    /** Replace the complete contents from a snapshot of *items*. */
    replaceAll(items: Iterable<T>): void;
    /** Move an item using pre-move source and destination indices. */
    move(fromIndex: number, toIndex: number): void;
    /** Remove all items. */
    clear(): void;
}

/**
 * Ordered serviced collection with expected O(1) captured-key lookup.
 *
 * Items remain caller-owned. Every mutation settles the ordered items,
 * captured keys, and key-to-index map before local and optional hub delivery.
 *
 * See spec/21-collections.md §§2.8–2.15 and ADR-0097.
 */

interface KeyedServicedObservableCollectionOptions<TKey, TItem> {
    readonly keyOf: (item: TItem) => TKey;
    readonly hub?: IMessageHub | null;
}
declare class KeyedServicedObservableCollection<TKey, TItem> implements ObservableMembershipSource<TItem> {
    #private;
    constructor(options: KeyedServicedObservableCollectionOptions<TKey, TItem>);
    get collectionChanged(): Observable<CollectionChangedMessage<TItem>>;
    get length(): number;
    at(index: number): TItem | undefined;
    toArray(): TItem[];
    [Symbol.iterator](): IterableIterator<TItem>;
    snapshot(): readonly TItem[];
    subscribeMembership(callback: () => void): Subscription;
    get(key: TKey): TItem | undefined;
    has(key: TKey): boolean;
    push(item: TItem): void;
    pop(): TItem | undefined;
    remove(item: TItem): boolean;
    removeAt(index: number): void;
    delete(key: TKey): boolean;
    /**
     * Apply native Array.splice normalization to an atomic candidate state.
     * Retained memberships keep their captured keys; inserted items are projected
     * once before commit and may reuse keys removed by the same operation.
     */
    splice(start: number, deleteCount?: number, ...newItems: TItem[]): TItem[];
    replace(index: number, newItem: TItem): void;
    setAt(index: number, newItem: TItem): void;
    replaceAll(items: Iterable<TItem>): void;
    move(fromIndex: number, toIndex: number): void;
    clear(): void;
    upsert(item: TItem): boolean;
}

/**
 * ObservableDictionary<TKey1, TKey2, TValue> — two-key observable dictionary.
 *
 * Entries are stored in insertion order. Four RxJS Subjects surface mutations:
 *   - itemAdded     — emits { key1, key2, value } on insert
 *   - itemRemoved   — emits { key1, key2, value } on remove
 *   - itemReplaced  — emits { key1, key2, newValue, oldValue } on replace
 *   - reset         — emits void on clear
 *
 * keys1 and keys2 are live ObservableList<TKeyN> views of the distinct Key1 /
 * Key2 values currently present, in insertion order of their first appearance.
 *
 * Null/undefined keys are not permitted; passing one throws Error.
 *
 * See spec/21-collections.md §4 and ADR-0025.
 */

/**
 * The element type carried in hub `CollectionChangedMessage` publications from
 * `ObservableDictionary`. Both keys and the value are included so subscribers
 * can recover the full identity of the mutated entry.
 *
 * C# equivalent: `KeyValuePair<(TKey1, TKey2), TValue>`
 * Python equivalent: `(key1, key2, value)` tuple
 * Per ADR-0006 each shape is flavor-idiomatic; per ADR-0009 the divergence is
 * catalogued and accepted.
 */
interface DictionaryEntry<TKey1, TKey2, TValue> {
    readonly key1: TKey1;
    readonly key2: TKey2;
    readonly value: TValue;
}
interface DictionaryItemAddedEvent<TKey1, TKey2, TValue> {
    readonly key1: TKey1;
    readonly key2: TKey2;
    readonly value: TValue;
}
interface DictionaryItemRemovedEvent<TKey1, TKey2, TValue> {
    readonly key1: TKey1;
    readonly key2: TKey2;
    readonly value: TValue;
}
interface DictionaryItemReplacedEvent<TKey1, TKey2, TValue> {
    readonly key1: TKey1;
    readonly key2: TKey2;
    readonly newValue: TValue;
    readonly oldValue: TValue;
}
declare class ObservableDictionary<TKey1, TKey2, TValue> {
    #private;
    /**
     * Create a new ObservableDictionary.
     * @param hub Optional hub. Pass null/undefined for standalone (no publication) mode.
     */
    constructor(hub?: IMessageHub | null);
    /** Emits when an entry is added. */
    get itemAdded(): Observable<DictionaryItemAddedEvent<TKey1, TKey2, TValue>>;
    /** Emits when an entry is removed. */
    get itemRemoved(): Observable<DictionaryItemRemovedEvent<TKey1, TKey2, TValue>>;
    /** Emits when an existing entry's value is replaced. */
    get itemReplaced(): Observable<DictionaryItemReplacedEvent<TKey1, TKey2, TValue>>;
    /** Emits void on clear. */
    get reset(): Observable<void>;
    /**
     * Live observable view of distinct Key1 values,
     * in insertion order of their first appearance.
     */
    get keys1(): ObservableList<TKey1>;
    /**
     * Live observable view of distinct Key2 values,
     * in insertion order of their first appearance.
     */
    get keys2(): ObservableList<TKey2>;
    /** Total number of entries. */
    get size(): number;
    /**
     * Insert or replace an entry.
     * Throws Error if key1 or key2 is null/undefined.
     * If the key pair already exists, the value is replaced and itemReplaced emits.
     * To guard against overwriting an existing entry, use {@link add} instead.
     */
    set(key1: TKey1, key2: TKey2, value: TValue): void;
    /**
     * Strict-insert an entry.
     * Throws Error if key1 or key2 is null/undefined.
     * Throws Error if the key pair already exists (use {@link set} for upsert behaviour).
     *
     * Mirrors `Add()` in C# and `add()` in Python, which both throw on duplicate keys.
     */
    add(key1: TKey1, key2: TKey2, value: TValue): void;
    /**
     * Remove the entry for (key1, key2).
     * Returns true if found and removed, false if absent.
     */
    delete(key1: TKey1, key2: TKey2): boolean;
    /**
     * Get the value for (key1, key2).
     * Returns undefined if absent.
     */
    get(key1: TKey1, key2: TKey2): TValue | undefined;
    /**
     * Try to get the value for (key1, key2).
     * Returns { found: true, value } if found, { found: false, value: undefined } if absent.
     */
    tryGetValue(key1: TKey1, key2: TKey2): {
        found: boolean;
        value: TValue | undefined;
    };
    /** Returns true if an entry exists for (key1, key2). */
    has(key1: TKey1, key2: TKey2): boolean;
    /** Remove all entries and emit reset. Does NOT fire per-entry itemRemoved events. */
    clear(): void;
    /**
     * Iterate entries in insertion order.
     * Each item is [key1, key2, value].
     */
    [Symbol.iterator](): IterableIterator<[TKey1, TKey2, TValue]>;
}

/**
 * IPageable capability: the implementer exposes a paged navigation surface
 * over its underlying data (CAP-022, ADR-0023).
 *
 * `pageSize` and `currentPageIndex` are mutable.
 * `pageCount` and `isPagingEnabled` are derived.
 *
 * Clamping contract (implementer responsibility, verified by CAP-022):
 * - Setting `currentPageIndex` outside `[0, pageCount-1]` must clamp to the
 *   nearest bound.
 * - Resizing `pageSize` must re-clamp `currentPageIndex` if out of range.
 * - All navigation methods are no-ops when already at the respective bound.
 *
 * When `pageSize` is 0 paging is disabled: every item fits in a single page
 * (`pageCount === 1`, `isPagingEnabled === false`).
 */
interface IPageable {
    /**
     * Number of items per page.  0 means "all items in one page" (paging
     * disabled).  Must not be negative; implementers may clamp negative
     * assignments to 0.
     */
    pageSize: number;
    /**
     * Zero-based index of the currently visible page.
     * Setting a value outside `[0, pageCount-1]` must clamp to the nearest
     * bound.
     */
    currentPageIndex: number;
    /**
     * Total number of pages.
     * Derived as `ceil(itemCount / pageSize)` when paging is enabled
     * (0 when the source is empty); 1 when paging is disabled (`pageSize === 0`).
     */
    readonly pageCount: number;
    /** `true` when `pageSize > 0`. */
    readonly isPagingEnabled: boolean;
    /**
     * Sets `currentPageIndex` to 0.
     * No-op when already at the first page.
     */
    moveToFirstPage(): void;
    /**
     * Decrements `currentPageIndex` by 1.
     * No-op when `currentPageIndex` is already 0.
     */
    moveToPreviousPage(): void;
    /**
     * Increments `currentPageIndex` by 1.
     * No-op when `currentPageIndex` is already `pageCount - 1`.
     */
    moveToNextPage(): void;
    /**
     * Sets `currentPageIndex` to `pageCount - 1`.
     * No-op when already at the last page.
     */
    moveToLastPage(): void;
}

/**
 * PagedComposition<TVM> — paged-view decorator for any source array or factory.
 *
 * Decorates any source (array, ObservableList, or lazy factory) with
 * paged-view semantics.  Implements IPageable (CAP-022, ADR-0023).
 *
 * The source is never mutated; this class computes a read-only slice on
 * demand.  If the source is an ObservableList or composite-style collection,
 * mutations are observed automatically so pageCount and items stay in sync.
 *
 * Arrays, other repeatable iterables, and factories stay live: every read
 * enumerates them again.  A source that is itself a one-shot iterator (a
 * generator object, for example) is materialized once at construction, as in
 * Python; pass a factory returning a fresh generator to keep it live.  Every
 * source must be finite, because pageCount needs its total length.
 *
 * pageSize = 0 disables paging: all source items appear on a single page
 * (pageCount = 1, isPagingEnabled = false).
 *
 * Empty source with pageSize > 0: pageCount = 0, currentPageIndex = 0,
 * items = [].  (Spec §5.4.)
 *
 * See spec/21-collections.md §5 and ADR-0023.
 */

type PagedCompositionSource<T> = readonly T[] | T[] | Iterable<T> | (() => Iterable<T>);
declare class PagedComposition<TVM> implements IPageable {
    #private;
    /**
     * @param source  Source array, iterable, or zero-arg factory.
     * @param pageSize  Initial page size (default 0 = paging disabled).
     *                  Finite integers are required; negative integers clamp to 0.
     */
    constructor(source: PagedCompositionSource<TVM>, pageSize?: number);
    get pageSize(): number;
    set pageSize(value: number);
    get currentPageIndex(): number;
    set currentPageIndex(value: number);
    get pageCount(): number;
    get isPagingEnabled(): boolean;
    moveToFirstPage(): void;
    moveToPreviousPage(): void;
    moveToNextPage(): void;
    moveToLastPage(): void;
    /**
     * The raw source passed to the constructor (never mutated). For a one-shot
     * iterator this is the exhausted iterator; `items` reads its snapshot.
     */
    get source(): PagedCompositionSource<TVM>;
    /**
     * The items on the current page.
     *
     * Returns all source items when paging is disabled (pageSize = 0).
     * Returns an empty array when the source is empty.
     */
    get items(): TVM[];
    /** Number of items on the current page (not the total source count). */
    get count(): number;
    /**
     * Observable that emits property names whenever they change.
     * Useful for bindings that need to react to page navigation or source mutations.
     */
    get propertyChanged(): Observable<string>;
    /** Unsubscribes from source observables. Idempotent. */
    dispose(): void;
}

type AsyncTask = (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>;
declare class AsyncRelayCommand implements IAsyncCommand {
    #private;
    constructor(task: AsyncTask | null, predicate: (() => boolean) | null, triggers: Observable<unknown>[], throwOnCancel: boolean);
    get isExecuting(): boolean;
    get canExecuteChanged(): Observable<void>;
    /**
     * Emit one re-evaluation notification without evaluating the predicate or task.
     * Valid while idle or in flight; a no-op after disposal.
     */
    raiseCanExecuteChanged(): void;
    /**
     * Surfaces a fault from the fire-and-forget `execute()` path (a rejecting task
     * that is not a cancellation). Await `executeAsync` to handle the error inline.
     * Cancellations never reach this channel. Completes on `dispose()`.
     */
    get errors(): Observable<unknown>;
    canExecute(): boolean;
    execute(): void;
    executeAsync(externalSignal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
    cancel(): void;
    /** Idempotent: subsequent calls are a no-op. */
    dispose(): void;
    static builder(): AsyncRelayCommandBuilder;
}
declare class AsyncRelayCommandBuilder {
    #private;
    constructor(task: AsyncTask | null, predicate: (() => boolean) | null, triggers: readonly Observable<unknown>[], throwOnCancel: boolean);
    task(fn: AsyncTask): AsyncRelayCommandBuilder;
    predicate(fn: () => boolean): AsyncRelayCommandBuilder;
    triggers(obs: Observable<unknown>): AsyncRelayCommandBuilder;
    throwOnCancel(value?: boolean): AsyncRelayCommandBuilder;
    build(): AsyncRelayCommand;
}

interface TokenPage<TVM, TToken> {
    readonly items: readonly TVM[];
    readonly nextToken: TToken | null;
}
interface TokenPagedCompositionOptions<TVM> {
    readonly autoConstructOnAdd?: boolean;
    readonly pagesEqual?: (left: readonly TVM[], right: readonly TVM[]) => boolean;
}
declare class TokenPagedComposition<TVM, TToken> {
    #private;
    constructor(fetchNext: (token: TToken | null) => Promise<TokenPage<TVM, TToken>>, options?: TokenPagedCompositionOptions<TVM>);
    get items(): TVM[];
    get currentToken(): TToken | null;
    get hasMore(): boolean;
    get loadMoreCommand(): AsyncRelayCommand;
    get refreshCommand(): AsyncRelayCommand;
    get collectionChanged(): Observable<CollectionChangedEvent>;
    get propertyChanged(): Observable<string>;
    dispose(): void;
}

/**
 * NullMessageHub — null-object variant of IMessageHub.
 *
 * See spec/03-messages.md §"Null variant" and ADR-0017.
 */

declare class NullMessageHub implements ITransactionalMessageHub {
    /** Shared singleton instance (the hub holds no state). */
    static readonly INSTANCE: NullMessageHub;
    private constructor();
    /** Empty observable — completes immediately upon subscribe. */
    readonly messages: Observable<IMessage>;
    /** No-op. */
    send(_message: IMessage): void;
    /** Execute a transaction body while continuing to publish nothing. */
    batch(transaction: () => void): void;
}

/**
 * NullDispatcher — null-object variant of IDispatcher.
 *
 * See spec/11-threading.md §"Null variant" and ADR-0017.
 *
 * Both schedulers are queueScheduler, which executes scheduled work
 * synchronously on the calling thread (no microtask, no macrotask hop).
 */

declare class NullDispatcher implements IDispatcher {
    /** Shared singleton instance. */
    static readonly INSTANCE: NullDispatcher;
    private constructor();
    readonly foreground: SchedulerLike;
    readonly background: SchedulerLike;
}

/**

/**
 * AsyncResourceVM — one cancellable asynchronously acquired presentation value.
 *
 * Spec: spec/23-async-resource-vm.md; ADR-0100.
 */

declare enum AsyncResourceStatus {
    Idle = "Idle",
    Loading = "Loading",
    Ready = "Ready",
    Error = "Error"
}
declare enum AsyncResourceRetention {
    DiscardPrevious = "DiscardPrevious",
    RetainPrevious = "RetainPrevious"
}
type AsyncResourceState<T> = Readonly<{
    status: AsyncResourceStatus.Idle;
}> | Readonly<{
    status: AsyncResourceStatus.Loading;
    value?: T;
}> | Readonly<{
    status: AsyncResourceStatus.Ready;
    value: T;
}> | Readonly<{
    status: AsyncResourceStatus.Error;
    error: unknown;
    value?: T;
}>;
interface AsyncResourceVMOptions<T> {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly loader: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>;
    readonly hub: IMessageHub;
    readonly dispatcher: IDispatcher;
    readonly hint?: string;
    readonly retention?: AsyncResourceRetention;
    readonly cleanupValue?: (value: T) => void;
}
declare class AsyncResourceVM<T> extends ComponentVMBase {
    #private;
    readonly loadCommand: AsyncRelayCommand;
    readonly reloadCommand: AsyncRelayCommand;
    readonly cancelCommand: RelayCommand;
    constructor(options: AsyncResourceVMOptions<T>);
    get type(): ViewModelType;
    get state(): AsyncResourceState<T>;
    load(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
    reload(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
    cancel(): void;
    protected _onDispose(): void;
}

/**
 * CompositeCommand — aggregates N inner commands.
 *
 * See spec/04-commands.md §Decorators and ADR-0012.
 */

declare class CompositeCommand implements ICommand {
    #private;
    readonly canExecuteChanged: Observable<void>;
    constructor(...inner: ICommand[]);
    canExecute(): boolean;
    execute(): void;
    /**
     * Make the composite inert (spec §8.4, ADR-0134). Idempotent. Notifies this
     * composite's `canExecuteChanged` subscribers once; subscribers of the inner
     * commands get nothing. The inner commands and their streams stay owned by
     * their creator.
     */
    dispose(): void;
}

/**
 * DecoratorCommand — wraps a single inner command with pre/post + extra-predicate.
 *
 * See spec/04-commands.md §Decorators and ADR-0012.
 */

interface DecoratorCommandOptions {
    preExecute?: () => void;
    postExecute?: () => void;
    extraPredicate?: () => boolean;
}
declare class DecoratorCommand implements ICommand {
    #private;
    constructor(inner: ICommand, opts?: DecoratorCommandOptions);
    get canExecuteChanged(): Observable<void>;
    canExecute(): boolean;
    execute(): void;
    /**
     * Make the decorator inert (spec §8.4, ADR-0134). Idempotent. Notifies this
     * decorator's `canExecuteChanged` subscribers once; subscribers of the inner
     * command get nothing. The inner command and its stream stay owned by its
     * creator.
     */
    dispose(): void;
}

type ConfirmDelegate = () => Promise<boolean>;
declare class ConfirmationDecoratorCommand implements ICommand {
    #private;
    constructor(inner: ICommand, confirm: ConfirmDelegate);
    get canExecuteChanged(): Observable<void>;
    /**
     * Observable that surfaces an error from the fire-and-forget {@link execute}
     * path — either the confirm delegate rejecting or a synchronous inner command
     * throwing. `execute()` is synchronous and runs the confirm gate
     * asynchronously, so it cannot propagate the way the base `RelayCommand`'s
     * task does; instead of swallowing the error it is emitted here (VMX-009).
     * An asynchronous inner command reports its own failures on its own error
     * channel, so they never arrive here. Await {@link executeAsync} to observe
     * failures inline. Completes on {@link dispose}.
     */
    get errors(): Observable<unknown>;
    canExecute(): boolean;
    /**
     * Fire-and-forget: starts the confirm flow and returns before it resolves.
     * Once confirmed, the inner command runs through its own `execute()`, so an
     * asynchronous inner keeps its failures on its own error channel and this
     * decorator does not watch its operation (spec §8.3.2). Await
     * {@link executeAsync} to sequence the flow inline.
     */
    execute(): void;
    /**
     * Awaits the confirm delegate and, when it resolves `true`, invokes the inner
     * command exactly once: an asynchronous inner (an `IAsyncCommand` or another
     * `ConfirmationDecoratorCommand`) through its `executeAsync()`, any other
     * inner through `execute()`. The promise settles when that invocation does,
     * so for an asynchronous inner it resolves when the inner operation
     * finishes. A confirm or inner failure rejects it unchanged and is not
     * emitted on {@link errors} (spec §8.3.2, ADR-0145). The inner keeps its own
     * admission and cancellation rules.
     */
    executeAsync(): Promise<void>;
    /**
     * Make the decorator inert and complete the {@link errors} channel (spec
     * §8.4, ADR-0134). Idempotent. Notifies this decorator's `canExecuteChanged`
     * subscribers once; subscribers of the inner command get nothing. A pending
     * confirmation that resolves later runs no inner command and emits nothing.
     * The inner command stays owned by its creator: an inner operation already
     * running is neither cancelled nor disposed.
     */
    dispose(): void;
}

/**
 * ModeledCrudCommands — Create / UpdateCurrent / DeleteCurrent helper.
 *
 * See spec/06-composite-vm.md §Modeled CRUD commands and ADR-0016.
 */

interface ModeledCrudCommandsOptions<M, VM> {
    current: () => VM | null | undefined;
    createNew: () => void;
    updateCurrent: (vm: VM) => void;
    deleteCurrent: (vm: VM) => void;
    confirmUpdate?: ConfirmDelegate;
    confirmDelete?: ConfirmDelegate;
    /**
     * @internal Phantom field to pin the `M` type parameter so it is not erased
     * by the TypeScript compiler. Never read at runtime; always undefined.
     */
    _model?: M;
}
declare class ModeledCrudCommands<M, VM> {
    #private;
    readonly createNewCommand: ICommand;
    readonly updateCurrentCommand: ICommand;
    readonly deleteCurrentCommand: ICommand;
    constructor(opts: ModeledCrudCommandsOptions<M, VM>);
    /**
     * Dispose the inner RelayCommands and any confirmation wrappers. Idempotent.
     *
     * The public update/delete commands may be `ConfirmationDecoratorCommand`
     * wrappers (when `confirmUpdate` / `confirmDelete` are supplied). Each wrapper
     * owns an `errors` Subject whose contract is to complete on dispose, so the
     * wrappers are disposed here alongside the inner relays (parity with
     * C#/Python). When no confirm hook is supplied the public command is the inner
     * relay itself, already covered.
     */
    dispose(): void;
}

/**
 * VM-backed modal result primitive.
 */
declare class ModalVM<T> {
    #private;
    constructor(cancellationResult: T);
    /** Result used when the modal is cancelled or disposed. */
    get cancellationResult(): T;
    /** Dismissal result, or `null` before dismissal. */
    get result(): T | null;
    /** True after dismissal or disposal. */
    get isDismissed(): boolean;
    /** Promise resolved when the modal is dismissed. */
    get completion(): Promise<T>;
    /** Complete the modal with `result`. Idempotent. */
    dismiss(result: T): void;
    /** Cancel the modal with `cancellationResult`. Idempotent. */
    dispose(): void;
}

/**
 * IDialogService contract — host-side modal interactions.
 *
 * See spec/19-dialogs.md and ADR-0029.
 */

/** Severity level for a notification presented via {@link IDialogService.notify}. */
type NotificationSeverity = "info" | "warning" | "error";
/** Describes a file-type filter for file-picker dialogs. */
interface FileFilter {
    /** Human-readable label, e.g. `"Image files"`. */
    readonly description: string;
    /** File extension patterns, e.g. `["*.png", "*.jpg"]`. */
    readonly extensions: readonly string[];
}
/**
 * Host-side service contract for modal interactions: file pick, confirm prompt,
 * and severity-tagged notify. See spec/19-dialogs.md §2.
 */
interface IDialogService {
    /**
     * Presents a file-open dialog. Returns the selected path, or `null` on cancel.
     * All parameters are optional.
     */
    pickFileToOpen(filter?: FileFilter | null, title?: string | null): Promise<string | null>;
    /**
     * Presents a file-save dialog. Returns the selected path, or `null` on cancel.
     * All parameters are optional.
     */
    pickFileToSave(filter?: FileFilter | null, title?: string | null, suggestedName?: string | null): Promise<string | null>;
    /**
     * Presents a confirmation prompt. Returns `true` when confirmed,
     * `false` when cancelled or dismissed.
     */
    confirm(message: string, title?: string | null): Promise<boolean>;
    /**
     * Presents a notification with the given severity. Severity defaults to `"info"`
     * when not supplied. Returns when acknowledged or dismissed.
     */
    notify(message: string, title?: string | null, severity?: NotificationSeverity): Promise<void>;
}
/**
 * Optional modal-capable dialog service. Existing IDialogService implementations
 * remain source-compatible; hosts that can present arbitrary VM-backed modals
 * implement this extension.
 */
interface IModalDialogService extends IDialogService {
    /** Presents a VM-backed modal and resolves with its result. */
    present<T>(modalVm: ModalVM<T>): Promise<T>;
}

/**
 * Fluent command composition helpers for VMx.
 *
 * Standalone named exports that are ergonomic shortcuts over the explicit
 * decorator constructors. They add no new behaviour.
 *
 * See spec/04-commands.md §9 and ADR-0027.
 */

/**
 * Returns a {@link ConfirmationDecoratorCommand} that gates execution of
 * `command` on the supplied async `confirmDelegate`.
 *
 * Equivalent to `new ConfirmationDecoratorCommand(command, confirmDelegate)`.
 */
declare function confirm(command: ICommand, confirmDelegate: ConfirmDelegate): ConfirmationDecoratorCommand;
/**
 * Returns a {@link ConfirmationDecoratorCommand} that gates execution of
 * `command` on {@link IDialogService.confirm} called with `prompt`.
 *
 * Equivalent to `confirm(command, () => dialogService.confirm(prompt))`.
 */
declare function confirmWithDialogService(command: ICommand, dialogService: IDialogService, prompt: string): ConfirmationDecoratorCommand;
/**
 * Returns a {@link CompositeCommand} where `other` executes *before* `command`.
 *
 * Equivalent to `new CompositeCommand(other, command)`.
 */
declare function precedeWith(command: ICommand, other: ICommand): CompositeCommand;
/**
 * Returns a {@link CompositeCommand} where `other` executes *after* `command`.
 *
 * Equivalent to `new CompositeCommand(command, other)`.
 */
declare function succeedWith(command: ICommand, other: ICommand): CompositeCommand;
/**
 * Returns a {@link DecoratorCommand} wrapping `command` with optional extra
 * `predicate`, `pre`, and `post` hooks.
 *
 * Equivalent to
 * `new DecoratorCommand(command, { extraPredicate: predicate, preExecute: pre, postExecute: post })`.
 *
 * Passing all `undefined`/`null` yields a semantically transparent decorator.
 */
declare function wrapWith(command: ICommand, predicate?: (() => boolean) | null, pre?: (() => void) | null, post?: (() => void) | null): DecoratorCommand;

/**
 * ComponentVM — non-modeled leaf viewmodel.
 *
 * See spec/05-component-vm.md §Variants.
 */

declare const optionHub$3: unique symbol;
declare const optionDispatcher$3: unique symbol;
/**
 * Options for the additive {@link ComponentVM.create} construction form
 * (ADR-0055 / VMX-020). A one-call alternative to the fluent
 * {@link ComponentVMBuilder}.
 */
interface ComponentVMOptions {
    /** Required VM name. */
    name: string;
    /** Required message hub. */
    hub: IMessageHub;
    /** Required dispatcher. */
    dispatcher: IDispatcher;
    /** Optional hint (default: ""). */
    hint?: string;
    /** Optional OnConstruct lifecycle callback. */
    onConstruct?: () => void;
    /** Optional OnDestruct lifecycle callback. */
    onDestruct?: () => void;
    /** Optional background-construction flag (default: false). */
    background?: boolean;
}
declare class ComponentVM extends ComponentVMBase {
    get type(): ViewModelType;
    static builder(): ComponentVMBuilder;
    /**
     * Constructs a {@link ComponentVM} from an options object in a single call —
     * an additive alternative to the fluent {@link ComponentVMBuilder}. Delegates
     * to that builder, so the required-field validation
     * ({@link BuilderValidationError} on a missing name/services) and the
     * resulting VM are identical to the fluent path.
     */
    static create(options: ComponentVMOptions): ComponentVM;
}
declare class ComponentVMBuilder {
    #private;
    constructor(from?: ComponentVMBuilder);
    name(value: string): ComponentVMBuilder;
    hint(value: string): ComponentVMBuilder;
    services(hub: IMessageHub, dispatcher: IDispatcher): ComponentVMBuilder;
    [optionHub$3](hub: IMessageHub): ComponentVMBuilder;
    [optionDispatcher$3](dispatcher: IDispatcher): ComponentVMBuilder;
    onConstruct(cb: () => void): ComponentVMBuilder;
    onDestruct(cb: () => void): ComponentVMBuilder;
    background(value: boolean): ComponentVMBuilder;
    /**
     * Chainable Wither that wires {@link NullMessageHub.INSTANCE} +
     * {@link NullDispatcher.INSTANCE} in a single call. Mirrors C#'s
     * `WithNullServices()` and Python's `with_null_services()` per
     * spec/10-builders.md / ADR-0035. Intended for tests, samples, and
     * exploration code; production VMs should call `services(hub, dispatcher)`
     * with real services.
     */
    withNullServices(): ComponentVMBuilder;
    build(): ComponentVM;
}

/**
 * ComponentVMOf<M> — modeled leaf viewmodel with settable model.
 *
 * See spec/05-component-vm.md §Modeled variant.
 */

declare const optionHub$2: unique symbol;
declare const optionDispatcher$2: unique symbol;
declare class ComponentVMOf<M> extends ComponentVMBase {
    #private;
    constructor(opts: {
        name: string;
        /** Defaults to `""`. */
        hint?: string;
        initialModel: M;
        /** Defaults to a hinter that returns `""`. */
        modeledHinter?: (m: M) => string;

        hub: IMessageHub;
        dispatcher: IDispatcher;

    /**
     * Constructs a {@link ComponentVMOf} from an options object in a single call —
     * an additive alternative to the fluent {@link ComponentVMOfBuilder}.
     * Delegates to that builder, so the required-field validation
     * ({@link BuilderValidationError} on a missing name/services) and the
     * resulting VM are identical to the fluent path.
     */

}
/**
 * Options for the additive {@link ComponentVMOf.create} construction form
 * (ADR-0055 / VMX-020). A one-call alternative to the fluent
 * {@link ComponentVMOfBuilder}.
 */
interface ComponentVMOfOptions<M> {
    /** Required VM name. */
    name: string;
    /** Required message hub. */
    hub: IMessageHub;
    /** Required dispatcher. */
    dispatcher: IDispatcher;
    /** Required model value. */
    model: M;
    /** Optional hint (default: ""). */
    hint?: string;
    /** Optional modeled-hint projection (default: () => ""). */
    modeledHinter?: (m: M) => string;
    /** Optional OnModelChanged callback. */
    onModelChanged?: (m: M) => void;
    /** Optional OnConstruct lifecycle callback. */
    onConstruct?: () => void;
    /** Optional OnDestruct lifecycle callback. */
    onDestruct?: () => void;
    /** Optional background-construction flag (default: false). */
    background?: boolean;
    /** Optional VM type (default: ViewModelType.Component). */
    vmType?: ViewModelType;
}
declare class ComponentVMOfBuilder<M> {
    #private;
    constructor(from?: ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>);
    name(value: string): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    hint(value: string): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    model(value: M): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    services(hub: IMessageHub, dispatcher: IDispatcher): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    [optionHub$2](hub: IMessageHub): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    [optionDispatcher$2](dispatcher: IDispatcher): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    modeledHinter(fn: (m: M) => string): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    onModelChanged(cb: (m: M) => void): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    onConstruct(cb: () => void): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    onDestruct(cb: () => void): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    background(value: boolean): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    vmType(value: ViewModelType): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    /**
     * Chainable Wither that wires {@link NullMessageHub.INSTANCE} +
     * {@link NullDispatcher.INSTANCE} in a single call. Mirrors C#'s
     * `WithNullServices<M>()` and Python's `with_null_services()` per
     * spec/10-builders.md / ADR-0035.
     */
    withNullServices(): ComponentVMOfBuilder<M>;
    build(): ComponentVMOf<M>;
}

/**

    get model(): M;
    get modeledHint(): string;
